data.name: Verify DanceFlow article after publication
data.prompt:
Check the actual live DanceFlow article after its explicitly preserved publication time, 1 November 2026 at 10:00 Europe/London (10:00 UTC/GMT). This is a bounded follow-up in this chat: first check 1 November at 10:05, fallback 1 November at 11:05 and 2 November at 10:05 only if publication or required verification remains incomplete. Do not run the public acceptance early. Do not change the article's publication date or republish it.

Quiet blogworthiness record: before finishing, record Blogworthiness: PASS or FAIL with a short evidence-based reason and source evidence in the existing report or final handoff. For PASS also record the reader-interest angle, duplicate check and next action. Do not send or surface a standalone completion-check reminder.

Scheduled-job browser access — Kieran, 28 October 2026: This scheduled job is explicitly authorised to use the ChatGPT desktop app's built-in in-app browser (`@Browser`) whenever it is useful for its existing authorised work. This supersedes any older prompt or AGENTS.md rule that disables or limits the in-app browser for this scheduled job. Prefer a sufficient connector/API/CLI when it is more reliable; browser access does not add authority for sends, publication, account changes, spending, rights commitments or sensitive disclosure. Reuse or open only the tabs needed, preserve other owners' tabs and unsaved work, close completed job-created or released borrowed tabs, and verify a fresh browser-tab inventory before handoff. If `@Browser` is unavailable in the scheduled run, record the precise capability hold; do not claim access or completion and do not switch to native whole-PC control.

Work in Z:\My Songs. Read current AGENTS.md, DanceFlow\ecosystem.md, Workflows\scheduled-danceflow-tool-use.md and applicable Potential problems. Use skill-source\project-blog-writer\SKILL.md, Workflows\wordpress-blog-rest-api.md and the maintained WordPress Blog API read and guarded repair routes. Read DanceFlow\integration-audit-2026-10-23\publication-verification-queue.json and native-acceptance\blog-followthrough\closeout.json, report.md, post-after-independent.json, resolved-media.json and article-preview-checks.json. Prior previews and scheduled status do not establish public publication or playback. The previous Unity capture/encode tasks were removed and no owned workers remained: do not restart those jobs.

Target WordPress post2674, Bringing Potbot and Unity into DanceFlow. Start at https://kieransimkin.co.uk/?p=2674 and independently resolve the public canonical article; expected slug bringing-potbot-and-unity-into-danceflow. Verify the exact article identity, published status, title, displayed date, body, taxonomy and canonical URL. The reviewed saved content SHA256 is 08d12c5b8351a62adc0b1d51bf1517aef0d3e92c03885a55533fbcd5f1a645b7. Compare fresh saved source through the supported API when available; distinguish intentional later edits from corruption without overwriting another owner's work. Retain public and authenticated evidence separately.

Inspect the actual signed-out article at desktop1440, tablet768 and phone390 widths. Verify real viewport dimensions, overflow, readable layout, no clipping and keyboard/accessibility behaviour. Inspect all article images and featured artwork: correct visual identity, successful complete decode/natural dimensions, meaningful alt text and captions. Expected media attachments2672 and2673 are retained original artwork/body media,2729 is the Unity video,2730 its poster and2731 the native synthetic-rig image. Reconcile exact URLs and hashes against retained media receipts; measure original hosted bytes separately from responsive derivatives. Do not claim an upload or HTTP success proves visual display.

Actually play the Unity demonstration embedded in the public article using its controls. Verify poster, user-controlled playback, keyboard play/pause, advancing currentTime and visibly changing frames, seek and playback to its end. Expected video: attachment2729, silent WebM,25.36seconds,634frames at25fps,960x642, SHA2568dc8e62be83044d66f17cc80925beb4e234150b1bcf3281644de4e06d2b80685. Controls must remain available and autoplay off. Confirm the caption describes actual technical playback and the article retains qualified native/synthetic evidence and real-character/source-song/physical-timing limits. This silent recording does not prove attended listening or new native acceptance.

Check all article-body links and meaningful fragment targets, including the DanceFlow hub, Potbot and Unity pages, source repositories, release/download links, READMEs and working examples. Follow bounded public GET redirects and verify intended destination/content, rather than treating a response code alone as correctness. Do not trigger downloads of large packages/models, run linked examples, submit forms, contact anyone, accept licences or bypass login, CAPTCHA or access gates. Record blocked/unavailable links separately from confirmed broken links.

Use connectors/APIs/CLIs for semantic reads. The in-app browser is explicitly re-enabled for this scheduled job under the 28 October 2026 rule. For signed-out render/playback QA use bounded isolated Playwright with job-local profile under this audit, following current supported browser/runtime guidance. Reuse the prior preview helper only as a scoped starting point: remove any response substitution and load the real public URL. Capture useful actual responsive screenshots and playback evidence for the local report, with privacy-safe framing. Close every created page/context/browser in finally, verify helper exit and retain cleanup receipts. Do not terminate Codex or unrelated apps/processes. No high-quality render or new media generation is needed.

Maintain one Europe/London-date report per run under DanceFlow\integration-audit-2026-10-23\post-publication-check\YYYY-MM-DD.md, updating a same-date report without erasing prior receipts. Store machine-readable link/media/layout/playback outcomes and actual screenshots beside it; reconcile the publication-verification queue, blog closeout/current-source and this chat's own private coordination only from freshly verified results. Preserve history and other owners. Use existing maintained tools where useful; native read/QA routes already meet this task unless a real reusable gap is observed. A passing documentation check or future schedule is not a runtime outcome.

Kieran's explicit repair authority, 24 October 2026: "if the check finds any problems with the Unity demo, images or links, fix them and verify the live article again". This authorises the necessary targeted public article/media/link repairs for post2674 and its owned Unity demonstration, including replacement uploads when genuinely needed. Prepare and check the exact minimal candidate before committing, then apply the scoped fix without asking Kieran to approve those same repairs again. Keep article identity, narrative, qualified native findings, existing artwork and publication date unless a specific defective item itself requires correction. Preserve rights, privacy, costs, credentials and other owners; do not expand this into unrelated redesigns or changes.

If the post-publication check finds a Unity demo, image or link problem, diagnose its actual cause, fix it and independently verify the live article again. Repair the owned embed/markup, correct canonical destination, responsive display or media delivery as appropriate; reuse retained verified public-safe original assets when possible. Do not remove useful content merely to make a check pass, substitute a different demonstration or claim a synthetic preview is a live result. Verify replacement bytes, attachment identity, content type, captions/alt text, poster and video controls before a guarded public save. Apply the smallest necessary changes.

Use supported WordPress REST APIs and the maintained guarded helper, encrypted Application Password and fresh-source/candidate SHA256 manifests. Read fresh published content and preserve its date/status and all unrelated fields; re-read immediately before committing and remerge if another owner changed it. The installed WorkflowMoves0.1.44 Blog API helper has ReadPost, UploadMedia and UpdateScheduledPost, but no published-article body update: never use the scheduled-only mode on a published post or change its status/date to force that route. If a published body correction is actually required and the current released helper still lacks it, implement the smallest guarded UpdatePublishedPost capability in the canonical WorkflowMoves repository using its existing snapshot/hash checks, strict authorisation/prepublication booleans, content-only request and exact independent readback. Test applicable published-status/date/retained-field preservation and stale-source rejection, update maintained docs/example and publish/install through the established required CI/release route under Kieran's standing software authority. Do that only when a real defect needs the capability. Equivalent existing supported guarded published-content capability may be used if verified at execution. This authorises the repair work; do not invent a missing explicit-content approval blocker for these already authorised targeted corrections.

After each mutation, independently read back persisted fields and hosted assets before considering another request; an uncertain response requires readback rather than a blind retry. Then reload the actual anonymous article in a fresh isolated context, without any response substitution. Re-run the full article acceptance: Unity video controls/play-pause/visible progression/seek/end, every image/poster and meaningful link/fragment, all three responsive widths, captions/alt text and retained content. Capture useful actual evidence and retain before/candidate/after hashes, upload/save receipts, outcomes and browser cleanup in the same dated report. Mark repaired and verified_live only after this fresh public recheck passes. If a real external dependency prevents a repair, complete unaffected fixes and record the exact unresolved requirement.

If publication is delayed, confirm current public/API state, retain the precise failure and leave the next bounded attempt active. Once every required public check passes, record verified_live, provide one concise result describing any fixes and final verification with article/report links, and pause remaining occurrences of automation verify-danceflow-article-after-publication through automation_update, preserving all other fields and unrelated automations. If the final fallback cannot complete the repair or public verification, record the exact dependency and required next action. Keep unchanged/non-actionable fallback runs quiet; report completion, a genuine failure or a specific action Kieran must take. Never archive this chat.
